passage_text: Researchers studied the effects of three different nutritional supplements on cognitive performance in adults aged 30–50. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group receiving a placebo, and three treatment groups receiving Supplement A, Supplement B, or Supplement C. Each group consisted of 40 participants. Cognitive performance was assessed using a standardized memory test administered at baseline and after 12 weeks of supplementation. The mean scores (out of 100) and standard deviations (SD) for each group after 12 weeks were recorded. The study aimed to determine which supplement, if any, produced the greatest improvement in memory scores relative to the control group. The results are summarized in Table 1 below.
stem: What is the mean score of the Supplement B group?
explanation: Correct: The table lists the mean score for Supplement B as 85.7. Why the others are wrong: A) 78.5 is the control mean. B) 82.3 is the Supplement A mean. D) 90.2 is the Supplement C mean.
trap: Students may confuse the mean score with the standard deviation or the control group mean.

stem: Which of the following best describes the design of the study?
explanation: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment or control groups, which is characteristic of a randomized controlled trial.
trap: Students may incorrectly identify the study as observational because it measures outcomes after an intervention.

passage_text: Researchers studied the effects of three different nutritional supplements on cognitive performance in adults aged 30–50. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group receiving a placebo, and three treatment groups receiving Supplement A, Supplement B, or Supplement C. Each group consisted of 40 participants. Cognitive performance was assessed using a standardized memory test administered at baseline and after 12 weeks of supplementation. The mean scores after 12 weeks were 78.5 (Control), 82.3 (Supplement A), 85.7 (Supplement B), and 90.2 (Supplement C).
stem: What is the overall mean score across all four groups combined?
explanation: Correct: All four groups have n = 40, so the overall mean is the simple average of the group means: (78.5 + 82.3 + 85.7 + 90.2)/4 = 84.2. Why the others are wrong: B) 85.1 does not follow from the table. C) 83.5 does not follow from the table. D) 86.0 is close to the mean of the three supplement groups alone (about 86.1), which leaves out the control.
trap: Averaging only the three supplement groups (about 86.1) and leaving out the control group.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data presented?

options.A: Supplement C had the lowest standard deviation
options.B: The control group had the largest sample size
options.C: Supplement C had the highest mean score
options.D: All groups had the same sample size

explanation: Correct: All groups have n = 40, so the statement that the control group had the largest sample size is false. Why the others are wrong: A) Supplement C has SD 4.5, the lowest. C) Supplement C has the highest mean (90.2). D) every group has n = 40.
trap: Assuming the control group is larger because it is the reference group, when every group has n = 40.

stem: What is the difference in mean score between Supplement C and the control group?
explanation: Correct: 90.2 - 78.5 = 11.7 points. Why the others are wrong: A) 3.8 is Supplement A minus control. B) 7.2 is Supplement B minus control. D) 4.5 is Supplement C minus Supplement B, not versus control.
trap: Comparing Supplement C with another supplement group instead of with the control group.
